walkthroughs.body_html: Romeo and Juliet was written by William Shakespeare around 1597. It's one of his most performed tragedies.
The play is set in Verona, Italy. Streets, a ball, a balcony and a tomb provide the key settings.
The Capulets (Juliet's family) and the Montagues (Romeo's family) carry an 'ancient grudge' — the feud drives the tragedy.

mcqs.q: What did Romantic poets value in nature?
options: Romantic poets just liked to write about pretty landscapes.
Nature as a source of spiritual insight and emotional truth, accessed through imagination — not picturesque scenery for its own sake.
Romantic poets believed nature was full of fairies and elves.

mcqs.q: Why must students distinguish the narrator from the author?
options: The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.
The narrator is a constructed voice within the text; the author is the real person who created it. Conflating them misreads irony, unreliable narration and persona.
The narrator's views are always the author's views.
It means it is wrong to write fiction.
The claim that judging a text by what the author 'intended' is fallacious — the text's meaning lies in the work itself, not the author's stated or guessed intentions.
It means it is wrong to write fiction.
It means authors can never make mistakes when writing.
